finding.claim: SQL injection in /search: the unauthenticated q query parameter is f-string interpolated into a LIKE clause, allowing an unauthenticated attacker to read arbitrary tables in shop.db via UNION/boolean/error-based extraction.
finding.sink: db.execute(f"SELECT id, name FROM products WHERE name LIKE '%{term}%'") at app.py:12; rows returned via jsonify at app.py:13

trace.note: GET /search route registered, no auth decorator
q read from query string with no validation
term concatenated into SQL text via f-string; no parameter binding
all result rows returned as JSON to the caller

finding.guards_checked: None on the path: no allow-list, escaping, length limit, parameter binding, or auth. Mitigating only: Python sqlite3 execute() refuses multiple statements (no stacked writes/ATTACH), load_extension disabled by default, injection confined to a SELECT (read-only). Fix: parameterize with (f"%{term}%",).

verdict.guard_found: None effective. The /search route (app.py:9) has no auth decorator. q is read unvalidated at app.py:11 and f-string interpolated into SQL at app.py:12 with no parameter binding. The candidate's listed mitigations are real but do not stop read-only injection: sqlite3 execute() rejects multiple statements (so no stacked writes or ATTACH), and load_extension is off by default. A single SELECT with UNION, boolean, or error-based extraction still reads any table in shop.db, and the rows are returned as JSON at app.py:13. The parameterized routes at app.py:18 and app.py:25 do not apply to this path.
verdict.reason: The unauthenticated /search route at app.py:9 feeds the raw q parameter (app.py:11) into an f-string SQL query (app.py:12) and returns all rows as JSON (app.py:13), and nothing between them binds, allowlists, or authenticates the input, so an anonymous attacker can extract arbitrary tables with UNION-based SELECT injection.
